```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("oncology_sdm_lobo_2002"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("oncology_sdm_lobo_2002"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1208/ps040442> (open access in PubMed Central,
  PMC2751331)

`oncology_sdm_lobo_2002` is a pharmacodynamic building block: it has no
pharmacokinetics of its own. The drug concentration `Cc` and the starting
cell number `tumor_vol0` are inputs (the model's `depends` field), so the
model can be driven by a measured concentration profile, as here, or
appended to a PK model that supplies `Cc`.

# Population

Lobo and Balthasar exposed two murine cancer cell lines in culture, Ehrlich
ascites cells and sarcoma 180 cells, to methotrexate (MTX) for 24 hours at
0.19, 2.0, 14.0 or 140.0 ug/mL, then washed the drug out (Methods, pages
2-3). Cells (1000 Ehrlich ascites or 500 sarcoma 180 cells per well of a
96-well plate) were allowed to attach for 48 hours before MTX was added;
4 wells were used per concentration and viable cells were counted by MTT
assay for up to 24 days. The transit compartment model was fitted in ADAPT II
to the mean cell number of the 4 wells, all concentrations of one cell line
simultaneously. There are no between-well random effects.

The packaged model carries the Ehrlich ascites parameter set (Table 2). The
sarcoma 180 parameter set (Table 3) is reproduced below by overriding the
`ini()` values.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("oncology_sdm_lobo_2002")()$population`.

# Source trace

The per-parameter origin is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in
`inst/modeldb/therapeuticArea/oncology/oncology_sdm_lobo_2002.R`.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lkng` (net growth rate kng, 1/h) | log(0.02) | Table 2 (page 9), transit compartment; Results page 7 |
| `ltau` (mean transit time tau, h) | log(34.1) | Table 2 (page 9), transit compartment; Results page 7 |
| `lec50` (EC50, ug/mL) | log(0.1) | Table 2 (page 9), transit compartment; Results page 7 |
| `kmax` (maximum cell-kill rate Kmax, 1/h) | 0.29 | Table 2 (page 9), transit compartment; Results page 7 |
| `propSd_tumor_vol`, `addSd_tumor_vol` | 0.3, 50 | Not in the paper (ADAPT II variance model not reported); placeholders |
| `d/dt(tumor_vol) = kng*tumor_vol - transit4*tumor_vol` | n/a | page 3, dC/dt = kng*C - K4*C |
| `d/dt(transit1..4)` chain with `drugEffectTumorVol = kmax*Cc/(ec50 + Cc)` | n/a | page 3, dK1/dt = (K - K1)/tau ... dK4/dt = (K3 - K4)/tau; K = Kmax*M/(EC50 + M) |
| Sarcoma 180 override: kng, tau, Kmax, EC50 | 0.035, 30.0, 0.34, 0.32 | Table 3 (page 9) |

# Digitised Figure 4

Figure 4 of the paper (page 6) shows the observed mean cell numbers and the
transit compartment model fits for both cell lines. The figure is vector
graphics, so the published model curves and the observed means were read
from the drawing commands of the PDF page and converted to hours and cells
using the axis tick marks; they are not hand-digitised estimates. The file
holds every vertex of each published model curve and the centre of each
plotted symbol.

```{r load-data}
fig4 <- utils::read.csv(file.path("data", "oncology_sdm_lobo_2002_fig4.csv"))
conc_levels <- c(0, 0.19, 2, 14, 140)
conc_labels <- c("no MTX", "0.19 ug/mL", "2 ug/mL", "14 ug/mL", "140 ug/mL")
fig4$conc_f <- factor(fig4$conc, levels = conc_levels, labels = conc_labels)
pub_curve <- filter(fig4, source == "published model")
obs <- filter(fig4, source == "observed mean")

# Every published curve of a cell line starts at the same cell number, the
# value at the moment MTX was added. It is the model's tumor_vol0 input.
c0 <- pub_curve |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  group_by(cell_line) |>
  summarise(c0 = unique(cells), .groups = "drop")
c0
stopifnot(nrow(c0) == 2)
```

# Simulation

MTX exposure is a 24-hour step: `Cc` equals the bath concentration from 0 to
24 hours and is zero after the wash-out. It is supplied as a time-varying
input column with last-observation-carried-forward interpolation, so the
step falls exactly at 24 hours. The model has no random effects, so one
subject per concentration gives the typical (and only) prediction. The
residual error is not used: the comparison is on the `tumor_vol` state.

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("oncology_sdm_lobo_2002")

# One subject per MTX concentration; Cc steps to zero at the 24-h wash-out.
make_events <- function(c0, tmax) {
  grid <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, tmax, by = 0.5), 24)))
  ev <- expand.grid(time = grid, conc = conc_levels)
  ev$id <- match(ev$conc, conc_levels)
  ev$evid <- 0
  ev$Cc <- ifelse(ev$time < 24, ev$conc, 0)
  ev$tumor_vol0 <- c0
  ev[order(ev$id, ev$time), c("id", "time", "evid", "conc", "Cc", "tumor_vol0")]
}

# A model with no omega warns that every subject is identical; that is the
# intent here, so only that warning is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}

solve_typical <- function(model, events) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxSolve(model, events,
      keep = "conc", covsInterpolation = "locf",
      returnType = "data.frame"
    )),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
}

mod_sarcoma <- mod |>
  ini(lkng = log(0.035), ltau = log(30.0), kmax = 0.34, lec50 = log(0.32))

sim <- bind_rows(
  solve_typical(mod, make_events(c0$c0[c0$cell_line == "Ehrlich ascites"], 420)) |>
    mutate(cell_line = "Ehrlich ascites"),
  solve_typical(mod_sarcoma, make_events(c0$c0[c0$cell_line == "Sarcoma 180"], 270)) |>
    mutate(cell_line = "Sarcoma 180")
) |>
  mutate(conc_f = factor(conc, levels = conc_levels, labels = conc_labels))
```

# Replicate Figure 4

Solid lines are the packaged model; dashed lines are the published fits;
points are the observed means. Each simulated curve is drawn over the time
span of the corresponding published curve (the authors stopped counting once
a well exceeded the upper limit of the standard curve).

```{r figure4, fig.height = 7}
spans <- pub_curve |>
  group_by(cell_line, conc) |>
  summarise(tend = max(time), .groups = "drop")
sim_plot <- sim |>
  inner_join(spans, by = c("cell_line", "conc")) |>
  filter(time <= tend)

ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = sim_plot, aes(time, tumor_vol, colour = conc_f), linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = pub_curve, aes(time, cells, colour = conc_f), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_point(data = obs, aes(time, cells, colour = conc_f), size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~cell_line, ncol = 1, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.9) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since start of the 24-h MTX exposure (h)",
    y = "Viable cells per well",
    colour = "MTX",
    caption = "Replicates Lobo 2002 Figure 4.\nSolid: packaged model; dashed: published fit; points: observed means."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Quantitative comparison with the published fits

Every vertex of each published curve is compared with the packaged model at
the same time. The simulation is deterministic, so these numbers do not
depend on a random seed.

```{r compare}
compare <- pub_curve |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sim = {
    s <- sim[sim$cell_line == cell_line & sim$conc == conc, ]
    stats::approx(s$time, s$tumor_vol, xout = time)$y
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - cells) / cells)

compare_summary <- compare |>
  group_by(cell_line, conc_f) |>
  summarise(
    n_points = n(),
    median_pct_diff = round(median(pct_diff), 1),
    p90_abs_pct_diff = round(quantile(abs(pct_diff), 0.9), 1),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
knitr::kable(compare_summary, caption = "Packaged model vs published Figure 4 curves (% difference).")

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-transcribed rate constant or a wrong exposure window
  # shifts a whole curve by far more than this.
  all(abs(compare_summary$median_pct_diff) < 15),
  # Envelope across the whole curve, including the published spline's own
  # wiggle (see the untreated arms below).
  all(compare_summary$p90_abs_pct_diff < 25)
)
```

The treated Ehrlich ascites arms sit about 12% below the published curves.
That is the reporting precision of Table 2, not a transcription error: kng is
reported as 0.02 (one significant figure) and Kmax as 0.29, and the
cumulative cell kill is proportional to Kmax times the exposure time while
the regrowth is exponential in kng. The untreated arms differ by up to about
11% even though they are pure exponentials, because the published lines are
smoothed through few points rather than drawn from a fine grid.

```{r rounding}
# kng = 0.0204 h-1 still rounds to the published 0.02 h-1.
sim_kng <- solve_typical(
  mod |> ini(lkng = log(0.0204)),
  make_events(c0$c0[c0$cell_line == "Ehrlich ascites"], 420)
)
compare_kng <- pub_curve |>
  filter(cell_line == "Ehrlich ascites") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(sim = {
    s <- sim_kng[sim_kng$conc == conc, ]
    stats::approx(s$time, s$tumor_vol, xout = time)$y
  }) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim - cells) / cells) |>
  group_by(conc_f) |>
  summarise(median_pct_diff = round(median(pct_diff), 1), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(compare_kng, caption = "Ehrlich ascites with kng = 0.0204 1/h (rounds to the published 0.02).")
stopifnot(all(abs(compare_kng$median_pct_diff) < 6))
```

# Peak and nadir timing

```{r timing}
features <- function(time, cells, tend) {
  keep <- time <= tend
  time <- time[keep]
  cells <- cells[keep]
  early <- time <= 150
  late <- time >= 24
  data.frame(
    t_peak = time[early][which.max(cells[early])],
    peak = max(cells[early]),
    t_nadir = time[late][which.min(cells[late])],
    nadir = min(cells[late])
  )
}
treated <- spans |> filter(conc >= 2)
timing <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(treated)), function(i) {
  cl <- treated$cell_line[i]
  cc <- treated$conc[i]
  p <- pub_curve[pub_curve$cell_line == cl & pub_curve$conc == cc, ]
  s <- sim[sim$cell_line == cl & sim$conc == cc, ]
  fp <- features(p$time, p$cells, treated$tend[i])
  fs <- features(s$time, s$tumor_vol, treated$tend[i])
  data.frame(
    cell_line = cl, conc = cc,
    t_peak_pub = round(fp$t_peak, 1), t_peak_sim = fs$t_peak,
    peak_pct_diff = round(100 * (fs$peak - fp$peak) / fp$peak, 1),
    t_nadir_pub = round(fp$t_nadir, 1), t_nadir_sim = fs$t_nadir,
    nadir_pct_diff = round(100 * (fs$nadir - fp$nadir) / fp$nadir, 1)
  )
}))
knitr::kable(timing, caption = "Peak (first 150 h) and nadir (after 24 h) of the treated arms.")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(timing$t_peak_sim - timing$t_peak_pub) < 10),
  all(abs(timing$peak_pct_diff) < 10),
  all(abs(timing$t_nadir_sim - timing$t_nadir_pub) < 12),
  # Discussion (page 8): the transit model predicted nadir cell counts
  # 100 to 200 hours after MTX removal (removal at 24 h).
  all(timing$t_nadir_sim - 24 >= 100 & timing$t_nadir_sim - 24 <= 200)
)
```

# Statements in the text

```{r text-claims}
# Results, page 7: doubling times 34.6 h (Ehrlich ascites) and 19.8 h
# (sarcoma 180), estimated from kng.
doubling <- c(
  ehrlich = log(2) / exp(rxode2::rxode(mod)$theta[["lkng"]]),
  sarcoma = log(2) / 0.035
)
round(doubling, 2)

# Results and Discussion: immediately after the 24-h exposure, treated and
# untreated cell numbers did not differ.
ratio_24 <- sim |>
  filter(time == 24) |>
  group_by(cell_line) |>
  mutate(ratio_to_untreated = tumor_vol / tumor_vol[conc == 0]) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(conc > 0) |>
  select(cell_line, conc, ratio_to_untreated)
knitr::kable(ratio_24, digits = 3, caption = "Cell number at 24 h relative to the untreated arm.")

stopifnot(
  abs(doubling[["ehrlich"]] - 34.6) < 0.1,
  abs(doubling[["sarcoma"]] - 19.8) < 0.1,
  all(ratio_24$ratio_to_untreated > 0.97)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* The packaged model is the Ehrlich ascites fit (Table 2). Sarcoma 180
  (Table 3) is not a separate model file; it is reproduced here by
  overriding the four structural parameters.
* The starting cell numbers (`tumor_vol0` = 2789 Ehrlich ascites cells and
  1214 sarcoma 180 cells) are the common starting value of the published
  curves in Figure 4. The paper reports the seeding density (1000 or 500
  cells) 48 hours before MTX, not the cell number at the start of exposure.
* The residual-error parameters `propSd_tumor_vol` and `addSd_tumor_vol` are
  not from the paper, which fitted mean cell numbers in ADAPT II without
  reporting the variance model. They do not affect any result on this page.
* The observed means are those plotted in Figure 4 (every 48 hours). The
  Methods list a denser counting schedule (days 1, 3, 5, ...); only the
  plotted points are reproduced here.
* NCA does not apply: the model has no drug amounts or concentrations of its
  own, and its output is a cell number.

# Errata

No published erratum was found for this article. The reference previously
carried by the model file gave the pages as 212-222; PubMed and the article
itself give AAPS PharmSci 2002;4(4):E42 (article 42).
